Extend the 100 µL bromo acid series from 10/1 to 50/1. Its measured interval is already much broader than that of the corresponding tert-butyl ester at 10/1, making this a useful test of acid-versus-ester transfer.

At 10/1 methyl thioglycolate's measured interval is 4.88 mL wide; the 50/1 centers imply 27.64 mL. Test the predicted broadening at fixed preparation, with several unmeasured 20/1 and 50/1 rows depending on it.
Add a weak-eluent point to the dihydrocoumarin curve at the same 50 µL sample as its 10/1 label. This provides a cyclic ester comparison for the ketone and open-chain ester series.

Give the unmeasured iododimethylbenzene a first label at a ratio with a measured fluoroiodotoluene analog. One endpoint can establish whether the low-retention prediction transfers across its many eligible rows.
One label covers the unmeasured bromopropylbenzene series and tests the early-eluting prediction shared by its unmeasured chloro homolog at matched ratio, sample volume, solvent and flow.

Place a first label on ethyl 2-bromopropionate where related bromoesters have measured retention. This tests whether the model transfers the effect of ester and alpha-carbon branching without needing several loads of the new structure.

Complete the para aminoester's 50 µL series at 5/1, 2/1 and 1/1. This tests whether its response also flattens in stronger eluent without treating cross-isomer preparation differences as structural effects.

For iodophenol the 50/1 centers are near the observed 20/1 volumes despite weaker eluent and a larger sample. This tests a consequential extrapolation across halophenols without presuming which of those changes dominates.

The dibromododecylthiophene elutes early at both measured extremes, yet its 2/1 V2 center is 21.69 mL. Test the predicted interior peak at the same load as the neat-EA run; three 2/1 loads share that prediction.

Anchor the 20/1–40/1 chlorobenzoate rows with a ratio contrast at fixed 10 mL/min. Several 30/1 records differ only in flow, so one label informs that shared model input without assuming all flow-specific volumes coincide.

The parent acetophenone has only a neat-EA label. Measuring it at 20/1 supplies a common structural baseline for numerous substituted ketones, including the para-fluoro analog measured with the same PE loading solvent and sample volume.
At 50 µL this directly compares ethyl acetoacetate with its 20/1 V2 of 65.15 mL. The intermediate ratio informs several eligible 10/1 rows and helps distinguish ethyl from methyl ester responses.

At 1/1 the same recorded preparation gave V2 of 10.60 versus 20.79 mL at 5 versus 10 mL/min. Test whether that discrepancy persists at 10/1, where multiple target rows use the slower flow. This informs the pooled volume estimate, not a separately learnable flow effect.

batch_review: 32 unique eligible rows cover 32 structures. Ratio-only comparisons retain the recorded load, preparation and flow; comparisons with additional changes are marked accordingly. One preparation-volume contrast, one load contrast and one flow-only comparison address specific measured discrepancies. The aminoester follow-up uses one slot, and no wide quantile interval or historical error was treated as sufficient evidence on its own.
batch_strategy: Choose rows that can change predictions for several neighboring records: missing ratios on measured response curves, sparsely measured structures in well-represented chemical families, and preparation contrasts where the model predicts little change. Include early-eluting counterexamples so that retraining does not impose a uniformly steep response to weaker eluent.

hypothesis_updates.claim: At 5/1 under their recorded preparations, ethyl 3- and 4-aminobenzoate have later V2 than ethyl 2-aminobenzoate.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: A fixed-preparation para series tests transfer of the meta curve's shape without requiring identical absolute retention across isomers.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: The fixed-preparation meta series now answers the prior question: from 2/1 to 1/1, V1 fell by 7.05 mL and V2 by 5.45 mL. This does not change the measured 5/1 ordering. The corresponding within-para comparison remains open.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: How much do para V1 and V2 decrease from 2/1 to 1/1 at 50 µL sample, 500 µL DCM and 10 mL/min?

feedback_interpretation: The 20/1 oxime V2 of 45.58 mL lies between its 10/1 and 50/1 measurements; the 69.69 mL acquisition prediction was an overestimate, not a current residual. The 2/1 naphthaleneethanol result also establishes a substantial shift from 5/1. Those series need less immediate follow-up. In contrast, the bromobenzyl alcohol load discrepancy remains unresolved, the methoxybenzyl alcohol endpoints leave a large interpolation gap, and the dimethoxybenzaldehyde result calls for testing preparation dependence of V2 separately from V1.
